item.content:encoded: This is an unfair assessment because it only rings true for the supplement to the 001 proposal — located on a separate page entirely — not the 001 itself. Here, the introduction of "retirement proposals" as a means of examining prior canon regarding 001 while offering new ideas, the penultimate iteration introducing new deities, and the surreal detour of the ultimate iteration, are genuinely novel takes. I haven't seen these things done with the 001 slot before. You can certainly dislike what's here, but this is a misleading criticism that barely touches what is here.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My criticisms still stand.

Too much of this feels grounded in high-concept cleverness rather than a concrete narrative. The whole substance of the story can be boiled down to "isn't it fucked up that 001s are big and important?" without any attempt to break down why they're written that way. As a result, the piece doesn't work on its own, and little attempt appears to have been made to ensure a reader gets something out of this without needing to be grounded in nostalgia goggles and in-crowd amusement.

Moreover: this piece never could have worked were it not an 001. This isn't in the sense of, say, TWIE or Past and Future, because when it comes down to it they're not altogether different from the likes of 5555, 4231, or 4239. If you'll forgive me for going joyless mountain witch, most of the "draw" I got from this article was its meta nature.

The meta is essential to the article. At no point in the article do the plot points function without it, because they're not diagetically resolved. Answering the question of "Why is primacy self-important?" strictly necessitates a reliance upon the self-importance afforded out of universe.

And maybe this is coming from (according to my correspondence with the author) one of the few critters who figured the thesis early into reading the piece, but the central critique presented by the article isn't even that interesting. Of course 001s get self-important. Practically every site contest based around writing SCPs engenders a certain level of self-importance, because if I've learned anything from my decade with this site, gimmicks get people reading. And maybe not everyone wants to read World-Ender 9000, but there's a good chunk of people who want it to get the 9000 slot.

Edited because I felt my previous comment was too ambiguous.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
When I first read this, I didn't know what to think; I both loved and hated this article, because you get all this build up to a climax and then there is hidden text in the last iteration, but it throws you off a cliff into… nothing, because it ends.

There are a lot of great ideas, but they were merely mechanics to catalyze the story, and while the story had excitement it was difficult to find importance in much of it, and the "Protector of Records and Information Security" was how you write stellar drama, except… It doesn't bring you into drama, or conclude into anything. What's wrong here? I hated feeling like this was incomplete, and it felt like it was very incomplete.

There's an explanation in the 001 proposal itself, it's internally consistent, and I'm fine with it not breaking the status quo and the reader gets to have their own headcanon about how things work out if they do at all, but… It doesn't resolve the story, I don't know what the significance of… Maria was, how the conflict went down or how this needs to be a loop.

Here's to trying to solve the puzzle (yes, spoilers):

+ show block
– hide block

They "neutralized" the effects of SCP-001 by removing the ability for everyone to perceive the primal ordinal. That's smart, but then you make it to the bottom of the article, and Maria is calling to you about protecting information security.

If Maria really was an anomaly as is described in one of those offsets, it means from the moment you clicked into "For details regarding SCP-001-1, contact RAISA Director Maria Jones." from the first page, you're already interacting with the anomaly - we still don't know whether maria is the problem, or SCP-001-1 is, and neither sides seem to be winning.

This conflict leads to the following points:

(1) She is the protector, and Site-01 / O5-1 / SCP-001-1 was the anomaly. She won by doing the obvious, but that also means… When you contact her, she wouldn't have just emailed you the file which re-activates SCP-001, is she that stupid?

(2) She is the anomaly, and she won by beating the containment project developed to protect humanity from SCP-001-1 by removing primal ordinals, returning to normalcy while she continues to overpower the world, and is why we see her all over the place. But then why did she say "The anomaly has captured me."? This doesn't make sense.

(3) Placeholder has written many Pataphysics related things: http://www.scpwiki.com/placeholder-mcd-s-authorpage and if you consider the errors (maria's speech in the final iteration, hidden,) in the strictest sense, you can interpret it this way:

(4) "We are entwined. You perceive us, and so we are."
Maria exists because of the collective will of the authors for her to be the RAISA director - even though in-universe, it makes sense for O5-1 to take this role, in reality ever since authors began to write on the SCP Wiki for RAISA, her name always came up instead. This conflict is not between Maria and O5-1, but between the out-of-universe authors and in-universe foundation, while Site-01 has not been affected, because it only exists in-universe.

(5) "It corrupts our knowledge. You forget me, and so I fade."
SCP-001 is considered important by everyone because it's… a cool number I guess? When there's a new successful 001, audiences will always treat it as an important one, where successful 001s can alter long chains of canons because it has that power to build such a worldview. If this SCP-001 is considered canon by all audiences and authors stop using Maria as the director of RAISA but instead O5-1, then she will cease to exist.

(6) "We shall see it as nothing. And so it shall be nothing."
Maria suggests for SCP-001 to be ignored, and so the status quo can be preserved, and she wouldn't be destroied. She has a point: This conflict matters very little to us and we're not really gaining much by restoring her power back to O5-1. For normalcy to persist, all that needs to be done is for SCP-001-1 to be suppressed under her; because we are out-of-universe, it won't damage in-universe narrative consistency, so she lets us know the true nature of it when we contact her, but in-universe she would hide it from the foundation.

And so, this brings us back to the consensus reality:
(7) SCP-001 is irrelevant: There is no canon.
It does not matter whether Maria or O5-1 is the director of RAISA. By having collectively decided for Maria to be the director of RAISA, all documents can remain narratively consistent in that sense, and SCP-001 proposals can still be as important as they are now if we choose to.

This also gives a new light to the "If absolutely necessary" line in the initial page: In-universe researchers have no necessity in understanding this fact, while out-of-universe, without additional explanation there is no way an article that only has as much content as the initial page can survive as a 001 proposal.

EDIT: SCP Declassified hire me pls

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I feel like no individual iteration of this proposal properly builds on previous iterations in a meaningful way. Like, it doesn't help that I felt like I was reading file editing logistics, which without any clear stakes is not particularly engaging. There were times that it felt like this was trying to explain site lore just for the sake of expanding lore because I never understood what it had to do with the throughline of the article. The way it loops in other proposals and the heritage collection felt particularly superfluous to the themes of SCP-001 having specific anomalous properties regarding consensus reality (which still felt underdeveloped in context of the scope of this piece).

I get that the last iteration is a language gimmick intended to like, mimic reality destabilizing, but the way that you've decided to just remove the letter "a" entirely just makes it unpleasant to read.

To me there were only 2 moments when I felt like there was some tangible set of stakes/conflict, and that's during the phone call, and the back and forth between the archivist and the primordial. These are definitely the strongest parts of the piece, but neither are expanded upon in a meaningful way to actually carry that investment over across the rest of the article.

By the end of the article, I don't know what I am supposed to be invested in, and if there is a mystery I don't know what questions I am supposed to be asking.

-1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hello author,

I thought I had more time to respond to your request for crit but you've posted, so, it'll have to come here.

Crit lives within
Yeet

First thing is first: the formatting here is meticulous and I appreciate the care that was done to make this visually appealing. The theme and presentation of your proposal is clean. The green console thing on offset 1 is the only real bummer and it's short and doesn't require a lot of focus, so, that's fine.

Landing page
This doesn't say much. I'm understanding it's a landing page but right away you've set me up with a pretty shallow place to start. Because this is an 001 and because this page is very short most people will give you the benefit of the doubt and click on.

Any effects SCP-001 is implied to have caused have been reverted

Maybe? If we don't know what it is and it's theoretical I don't see how we can make this claim. Unless you mean to say everything we know of we have reverted.

any additional information concerning SCP-001 is irrelevant.

Semi-meme answer but, then why am I reading the rest of this?

that were inexplicably uploaded

An awful set of words for an SCP document.

but is ultimately of no significance.

Again, why am I reading about them then? Based on the rest of this article this is aggressively meta.

Offset 1
Collectively, this says many things but the information is generally redundant or is otherwise repetitive in the context of the two pages we've seen so far. The way you're throwing around implications about restructuring of reality and just non-chalantly "Reversing" the implications is…well I think you get my point. The way this is being treated so far feels extremely shallow but I am willing to press on.

In this state, SCP-001 appears to be effectively contained as there is little evidence to suggest that it is capable of amplifying itself.

'little evidence' and 'no evidence' are extremely important distinctions

These patterns of missing and/or conflicting evidence are thought to manifest as a result of CK-class reality-restructuring events

This is a can of worms dramatically out of line with everything else you've said to this point.

Offset 2
This says a fair bit more than the first Offset does but I am still left with a very aimless taste in my mouth. Not to use overly-dramatic language but the endless circle here has really worn my patience quite thin.

An alleged image of SCP-001-A.

No, it's actually an image. It's alleged that they are SCP-001-A

is the Director of RAISA and has been for over a decade.

Are you wording it like this for a reason? Why not put a date?

SCP-001 proposal file had been replaced with a single, unformatted document that read "Maria Jones does not exist".

For me, this has lost any potential impact by being non-chalantly buried here in this paragraph.

UNKNOWN: I think it's devouring me now.

People don't speak like this.

Offset 3
The presentation here is better than the last iteration, I feel more meaning, but this is another incremental step. It feels like it's rehashing the other offsets yet again with very little build. My frustration about a lack of obvious direction (or even the anticipation of one) has gone.

series of documents that are inexplicably appended to the SCP-001 file location.

This is so much better wording than the first time you tried to say this. Unfortunately I can't tell if that's deliberate or not, or merely a consequence of the formats and styles you're trying to recreate/copy.

(known as Lesser Archivists))

You have a double close parenthesis here.

this form thinks we are getting the hang of this.

This is really tone breaking.

Personnel are to be reminded of the significance of SCP-001.

Too overtly meta.

Offset 4
This format is so actively off-putting to me I have no comments. Red on black is sharp, so you've got that going for you.

Overall the progress here is far too incremental and in spite of that, only goes for 4 fairly short offsets before stopping. This is very wide but hasn't given me the impression of much depth unless I come into this accepting the very same position you, the author, have about 001 proposals.

This isn't for me and I am not sure I see a satisfying way to turn the format you have presented into something I would upvote. I respect your time and dedication and ambition to tackle this but I'm giving the article a -1 for the above merits.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Beyond the technical jargon and flashy presentation, there is very little actual substance to this article. The story itself is awkward and difficult to follow, and the commentary it tries to provide simply falls flat. Conceptually, it basically feels like it's trying to one-up the other 001s by making its whole gimmick the explanation of the 001 slot as a whole, and the entire thing uses other 001s, as well as the 001 slot itself, as a crutch. Especially when the intended message is considered, this sort of support is baseless and ends up falling flat.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This feels like it really suffers from mistaking 'sounding smart' with 'being interesting'. None of the elements come together in an interesting manner and I'm left just feeling…drained by it. It feels like an homage to every other 001 without really doing anything interesting with it; and the one time you attempt something fun (the removal of the concept of unity), you format it in such a way that it's a pain to read (even with highlighting the page) and ultimately shallow. This feels like it's attempting to ape the ouroboros cycle without the narrative weight or quality of writing it achieved.

item.title: placeholder
item.content:encoded:
This is my love letter to 001 proposals, and my critique of the significance we put on them as a community. Yes, it has elements of many other proposals in it; this is by design. Each of these iterations includes concepts and tropes of proposals that I admire, with my own spin put on them.

As for what is literally happening here, I feel that all of the puzzle pieces are laid out, and anyone who is interested can discover a valid interpretation if they dig in enough. That being said, the precise details and mechanics of the anomaly/Jones construct and how it comes to be are not essential to the narrative and its intended meaning.

Thank you very much to everyone who gave critique on this. There were so many critters it's hard to remember them all, but each of them significantly contributed to my process of writing this.

Special thanks to HarryBlank and Yossi, who stuck with me through much of the process and reread the thing many times.
